**No U.S. president signed an "Antarctic Statehood Act." The question rests on a false premise. Antarctica is not a U.S. state, and I found no such law or bill.**

I used two searches and did not open any of the pages. The claims below rest on search-result summaries.

- I found no record of an "Antarctic Statehood Act" or of any proposal to make Antarctica the 51st state.
  - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/51st_state
  - https://www.quora.com/If-Antarctica-became-the-51st-state-what-would-it-mean-for-each-of-the-research-stations-on-the-continent
  - The Quora link is a hypothetical discussion, not a source for any law.
- The closest real item is a Greenland bill, not an Antarctic one. Rep. Randy Fine introduced it to enable annexing Greenland and admitting it as a state.
  - https://thehill.com/homenews/house/5685118-fine-introduces-greenland-bill/
  - https://www.newsweek.com/greenland-could-become-51st-state-under-proposed-bill-11349217
- The one Antarctic law the search surfaced for the U.S. is the Antarctic Conservation Act, which deals with environmental protection, not statehood.
  - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antarctic_Conservation_Act
- The Antarctic Treaty was signed in 1959 and entered into force in 1961. It covers the area south of 60°S.
  - https://2009-2017.state.gov/t/avc/trty/193967.htm
- Article IV of the treaty freezes territorial claims. No new claim or enlargement of an existing claim can be asserted while the treaty is in force.
  - https://2009-2017.state.gov/t/avc/trty/193967.htm
  - https://www.diplomacyandlaw.com/post/who-owns-antarctica
- Seven nations hold claims: Argentina, Australia, Chile, France, New Zealand, Norway and the UK. The U.S. recognizes none of them and has no claim of its own.
  - https://www.diplomacyandlaw.com/post/who-owns-antarctica
  - https://thelegalguide.org/who-legally-owns-antarctica-sovereignty-antarctic-treaty/

My searches can't prove that no such bill exists anywhere. They turned up no trace of one, and the treaty framework makes U.S. statehood for Antarctica legally implausible.
